limitations: Per-process GPU memory cannot be read from outside this container (nvidia-smi reports host pids); it is capped (torch allocator fraction) and reported inside every Python process of a GPU job by an interpreter hook injected through PYTHONPATH. A job that replaces PYTHONPATH inside its own command (e.g. `bash -c 'PYTHONPATH=x python ...'`) or a non-Python CUDA program is detected as holding a GPU context but is not metered; the allocator cap covers torch's caching allocator, not the CUDA context itself (~200-450 MB per process).

Enforcement is by sampling (1 s by default): RAM and disk can overshoot by what a job allocates or writes within one interval before it is killed (probe: 300 MB grant, 304-398 MB at kill when allocating 1 GB/s at 0.25 s sampling).

Older copies of slots.py in other worktrees share the ledger (entries stay compatible) but neither the FIFO queue nor the stored budget: until every worktree runs this version they can still overtake queued requests and use their own environment budget.
GPU time is accounted as seconds during which a process holds a CUDA context (an upper bound of kernel time); per-process SM utilisation is not observable from this container.

Class 4 (semantic generalists) is not bound to any runtime in the tree (population.register_class_runtime has no caller), so no profile has four acting classes; V.1 and SP-13.1 fail until CORE-POP/CORE-SEM bind it.

crucible.civ.generate fails at 87a6c54 (missing 'space' dependency) and the population tick fails there (KeyError 'items'); the integration fix (c5c/w3-intfix) repairs both. All civ-world measurements of the gate tests therefore fail on this branch alone.

The event-driven speedup is the ratio of decision-policy compute (dense per-tick evaluation of every eligible individual vs evaluation of the activated individuals) measured by observers of one world, not of two differently scheduled worlds; the world-level CPU ratio is reported next to it.

The estimated cohort mode is deliberately simple (exchangeable cohorts, per-kind attractiveness, no contact graph); its errors are measured and reported, and it is never used to produce world outcomes.

Candidate retrieval (13.6) was measured with an inverted-file index on synthetic clustered vectors: 1.2x faster than all-pairs at 1M items with recall 0.83 - the in-tree recommenders' candidate pools were not separately benchmarked.

kernel.py: World.__init__ registers with crucible.scale.governor and World.close releases (2 small insertions); substrate/inference.py wraps fn() of recorded() in governor.inference(). Both are no-ops outside a governed job.

The shared ledger /tmp/crucible-slots now has budget.json (cpus 9, gpu 24000 MB, jobs 12 (raised from 8 with a recorded reason: the CPU budget binds), ram 69,481 MB, default RAM ceiling 46,321 MB for undeclared jobs, gpu_jobs 4, inference 16, worlds 512, disk 40,000 MB). Change it only with `python -m crucible.scale.slots --set-budget k=v --reason ...`.

Official runs of the performance gates should be launched inside one governed job sized for the suite (README: --cpu 6 --gpu-mb 2000 --ram-mb 64000 --disk-mb 12000); the tests nest their runs in that job's ledger. Runs of a clean commit are cached per commit (CRUCIBLE_BENCH5_CACHE) so the separate gate files share one suite.
